the_news.text: Starting Oct. 9, 2026, Google will limit free Gemini app users to Flash-Lite only (no Flash or Pro) and remove Pro from AI Plus ($4.99/month) subscribers on a date Google will email them, per an updated Google support page; AI Pro ($19.99/month) is the cheapest plan that keeps all three models.

why_it_matters.text: Free users lose the model picker's Flash and Pro options, and anyone relying on Pro (coding, studying, large files) on free or AI Plus must pay $19.99/month for AI Pro to keep it, an extra $15/month ($180/year) over AI Plus per Yahoo's math.

The change touches a very large user base: Google says Gemini passed 1 billion monthly users in August (Google's own claim as relayed by Yahoo), and PCMag ties it to rising storage and component costs, noting Google has not itself been quoted giving that reason.

pages.title: Using Google Gemini for Free? You're Losing Some Models Later This Week
pages.text:
If you’re not paying for Gemini, you are about to lose access to the chatbot’s Flash and Pro models.As spotted by 9to5Google, Google has updated a support page to note that it is restricting what Gemini models free and AI Plus users can use. On Oct. 9, free users will lose access to both Gemini’s 3.6 Flash and 3.1 Pro models, while AI Plus subscribers will soon be notified via email that they’re losing access to the 3.1 Pro model.Google’s Gemini models come in three tiers. Flash-Lite is the lightest and fastest, Flash is the all-around middle option, and Pro is the most advanced.

So far, free users have had limited access to all three models. Once the new limits take effect, they will only be able to access the 3.5 Flash-Lite model. The 3.6 Flash model unlocks with Google’s $4.99-per-month AI Plus plan, while the 3.1 Pro model unlocks with a $19.99-per-month AI Pro subscription. Students, meanwhile, remain eligible for a year of Google’s AI Pro plan for free.

(Credit: Google)

Google also notes that you’ll soon be able to choose the level of effort each model puts into your queries, between low, medium, or high. “This will increase the model’s ability to complete tasks and provide more thorough answers to queries, but will also use more of your limit,” the company says.

Recommended by Our Editors

Compared with the free plan, Google’s AI Plus and Pro plans offer 2x and 5x Gemini usage limits, respectively. The company, however, doesn’t explain how it calculates these limits. “Calculation of your usage will factor in the complexity of your prompt, the features you use, and the length of your chat,” it says.This is the second time Google has overhauled its AI plans this year. The latest changes come as storage and component costs continue to rise, potentially directly affecting the company's AI infrastructure spending.

pages.title: Google to end free access to Gemini Flash and Pro models — Engadget
pages.text: Google will end free access to the Gemini Flash and Gemini Pro models in the app and web version of its chatbot on October 9. For users without a subscription, all requests will be handled by Gemini Flash-Lite, the company’s most economical model, Engadget reports.Which models will remain freeCurrently, free users can choose from three models in a drop-down menu in the app or next to the input field in the browser. After the change, this choice will disappear: only Flash-Lite will remain for free accounts. Gemini Flash is more powerful than Lite, while Gemini Pro is designed for more complex tasks and deeper reasoning.More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.Changes for subscribersUsers of the cheapest Google AI Plus plan, which costs $5 per month in the United States, will also lose access to Gemini 3.1 Pro. Google describes this model as suitable for complex math tasks, programming, and working with text, files, images, and video. The company notes that users who need such capabilities may have to upgrade to the Google AI Pro plan, which costs $20 per month in the United States. AI Ultra, with higher limits, costs at least $100.The company is also introducing effort-level settings for each model — low, medium, and high. A higher level is expected to provide more detailed responses but use up the usage limit faster. AI Ultra subscribers will receive the Deep Think option and, after its general launch, access to Gemini 4 Argon, which is currently available to members of the Fairwind program for governments and verified partners.

pages.title: Google Gemini Free Users Lose Flash and Pro Oct. 9. Here’s What It Costs to Keep Them
pages.text: Google's free Gemini app is about to have a much shorter menu. Beginning Oct. 9, people using Gemini without a paid AI subscription will lose access to Flash and Pro. Flash-Lite will be the only model available to them. Google AI Plus subscribers are losing Pro as well, although Google says those customers will receive an email with the date their access changes.The price difference gets your attention quickly. Google currently lists AI Plus at $4.99 a month and AI Pro at $19.99. A Plus subscriber who regularly uses Pro and wants to keep it would be looking at another $15 a month, or $180 over a year, at current prices.If you have never opened Gemini's model picker, you may not care. If Pro is where you go for coding, studying, large files or the sort of research project that starts innocently and somehow leaves you with 14 browser tabs open, I would check your account before Oct. 9.Google says Gemini passed 1 billion monthly users in August, making this a change plenty of people could notice.What changes on Oct. 9Google's new lineup leaves free users with Flash-Lite. AI Plus keeps Flash-Lite and Flash. Pro will require AI Pro or AI Ultra once the changes reach an account.PlanCurrent U.S. priceFlash-LiteFlashProFree$0YesNoNoAI Plus$4.99/monthYesYesNoAI Pro$19.99/monthYesYesYesAI UltraFrom $99.99/monthYesYesYesGoogle describes Flash-Lite as its speedy model for everyday work such as summarizing and brainstorming. Flash handles a wider range of problems and adds more reasoning capability. Pro is Google's most advanced model, with stronger performance on complex math, coding, studying, files, images and video.I wouldn't pay $20 a month simply because the word "Pro" disappears from a menu. If most of your Gemini use involves summaries, quick questions, trip ideas or cleaning up an email, Flash-Lite may do everything you need.People already leaning on Pro have a harder decision. Google built it for the more demanding work, and AI Pro will soon be the cheapest plan that keeps all three models.The $19.99 price lands in an interesting spotConsumers are getting increasingly comfortable paying for AI. Menlo Ventures surveyed 5,067 U.S. adults with Morning Consult in July and found 55% of AI users pay for at least one AI product. Among people who pay, the typical monthly spend was $20 to $49. The research also found payers use AI daily at nearly twice the rate of non-payers.Someone who opens Gemini a few times a month is probably going to live with Flash-Lite. Someone using AI every day for work, school or a side business may already think of $20 as another software bill. Still, subscriptions add up. AI Pro at $19.99 costs nearly $240 a year. Moving up from AI Plus adds $180 to that annual bill.Before paying it, I'd spend a week paying attention to the model you actually select. If you keep reaching for Flash, the $4.99 Plus plan still gives you access to it after the change. If you keep reaching for Pro, you have your answer.AI Plus customers may have more timeOct. 9 is the start date Google gives for users without an AI subscription. AI Plus customers have a different schedule. Google says Plus subscribers should receive an email explaining when the changes take effect for their account.So if you pay for AI Plus and Pro is still available after Oct. 9, don't assume Google abandoned the change. Your account may have a later date. I also wouldn't upgrade before reading that email. There is no prize for being the first person to volunteer for a larger monthly bill.College students should check Google's free offer firstEligible U.S. college students have a much easier decision. Google is offering them one year of AI Pro at no charge, a plan it values at $19.99 a month. The offer can be redeemed through Dec. 31, 2026. Google requires a valid payment method, and the subscription begins charging $19.99 a month after the free year unless it is canceled.If you qualify, check that offer before paying for Pro yourself. A free year at Google's normal price is worth almost $240.Check which Gemini model you actually use before paying moreThe easiest thing you can do before Oct. 9 takes about ten seconds. Open Gemini. Look at the model picker. See what you have been using.If Flash-Lite is already doing most of the work, keep your money. If you rely on Flash, AI Plus keeps it for $4.99 a month. If Pro has become part of your routine, AI Pro is where Google is putting it.Right now, many users can open that menu and choose among Flash-Lite, Flash and Pro. Soon the choices you see will depend much more on the plan attached to your account.And before spending another $180 a year, it is worth knowing which one you were actually using.

If you use Gemini in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, or elsewhere in the Middle East, the change to watch is the model limit taking effect on Oct. 9. The available information doesn’t confirm local subscription prices in AED, SAR, or EGP.

Google’s Gemini models come in three tiers. Flash-Lite is the lightest and fastest, Flash is the all-around middle option, and Pro is the most advanced.

So far, free users have had limited access to all three models. Once the new limits take effect, they will only be able to access the 3.5 Flash-Lite model. The 3.6 Flash model unlocks with Google’s $4.99-per-month AI Plus plan, while the 3.1 Pro model unlocks with a $19.99-per-month AI Pro subscription. Students, meanwhile, remain eligible for a year of Google’s AI Pro plan for free. Students in Egypt and Saudi Arabia can also check the regional details of Google Gemini Pro’s free student offer.

(Credit: Google)

Google also notes that you’ll soon be able to choose the level of effort each model puts into your queries, between low, medium, or high. “This will increase the model’s ability to complete tasks and provide more thorough answers to queries, but will also use more of your limit,” the company says.

Compared with the free plan, Google’s AI Plus and Pro plans offer 2x and 5x Gemini usage limits, respectively. The company, however, doesn’t explain how it calculates these limits. “Calculation of your usage will factor in the complexity of your prompt, the features you use, and the length of your chat,” it says.

Google Gemini plan pricing and availability in the UAE and Saudi Arabia

The plan prices in this report are listed in US dollars: $4.99 per month for AI Plus and $19.99 per month for AI Pro. No verified UAE, Saudi Arabia, or Egypt prices are available here, so we haven’t added AED, SAR, or EGP conversions. Check the Gemini app or your Google account for the price shown for your location.

pages.text:
Following the compute-based usage change in May, Google will soon introduce limits on which Gemini models free users and AI Plus subscribers can access.

According to an updated support document this week, Gemini app users without a Google AI subscription will be limited to the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. Starting October 9, users who do not pay for Gemini will no longer be able to access (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

Meanwhile, AI Plus subscribers will be limited to Flash-Lite and Flash, with Pro no longer available. These $4.99 per month users will “receive an email that explains when these changes will take effect.”

pages.title: Google Removes Free Access To Gemini Flash And Pro On October 9
pages.text:
Free Gemini users will only be able to use Gemini Flash-Lite.

Kenneth Cheung/Getty Images

Google has revealed changes to its Gemini apps and website on its support page, which could impact how you use the AI chatbot if you're not paying for a subscription. Starting on October 9, you will no longer be able to access the Gemini Flash and Pro models if you're on a free account. At the moment, you'll see three options in the drop-down menu at the top of the app or right next to the text box on desktop. But in a few days, all your free inquiries on Gemini will use Flash-Lite, Google's most cost-effective model. Flash is a step up from Lite, while Pro was designed for advanced reasoning and more complex tasks.

If you're paying for Google AI Plus, the company's cheapest subscription tier that costs $5 a month in the US, you will be losing access to the Gemini 3.1 Pro model, as well. Google says Pro excels at dealing with complex math and coding prompts, and it has a "deeper understanding across text, files, images and videos" than other models. In other words, if you use Gemini for coding or as a study aid and need it to digest loads of documents and other materials, you may need to start paying for an AI Pro plan. Google AI Pro costs $20 a month, while AI Ultra, which has higher usage limits, will cost you at least $100 a month.

In addition to those changes, Google is adding "effort level" options for each model. You'll be able to choose between low, medium and high, which provide models with increasing abilities to complete tasks. The higher the level, the more thorough the answers, though it will also eat more of your limit. If you pay for an AI Ultra subscription, you'll get access to a Deep Think option if you need to tap into Gemini's maximum capabilities.

AI Ultra subscribers will also get access to Gemini 4 Argon when it rolls out to the general public. Right now, it's only available to members of Google's Fairwind Program for governments and trusted partners.

pages.title: Gemini Apps limits & upgrades for Google AI subscribers
pages.text:
Gemini Apps have compute-based usage limits that determine how much you can interact with Gemini tools and features. These limits factor in the complexity of your prompt, the models and features you use, and the length of your chat. Your limit refreshes every 5 hours until you reach your weekly limit.

You can upgrade to a Google AI plan for expanded access to features and models in Gemini Apps. Gemini Apps upgrades are part of select Google One paid plans for personal accounts. Learn more about availalble subscriptions.

Important: This article is for users managing Gemini Apps for a personal Google Account. If you’re using a work or school Google Account, learn more about using Gemini Apps with a work or school account.

What you need

To use Gemini Apps with a Google AI plan in most countries, you must be 13 (or the applicable age in your country) or over.

To use Gemini Apps with a Google AI plan in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom, you must be 18 years of age or older.

Some features may not be available for users under the age of 18 or 13 (or the applicable age in your country). In the help center, you will find additional information about age requirements.

What you can do when you reach a usage limit

If you have a Google AI subscription and reach your limit, you can continue your conversation with Flash-Lite.

If you reach your five hour or weekly usage limits you can upgrade to a Google AI subscription with higher limits or wait until your model limit is refreshed. Learn how to upgrade.

Usage limit changesLimits may change without notice, including due to capacity constraints. When there’s a large increase in activity in Gemini Apps, we may change limits to maintain a high standard of quality.

Important:

For users without a Google AI plan, some features that require more compute resources, like Deep Research, may be unavailable during periods of high demand.

If capacity changes, limits for users without a Google AI plan may be limited before users with a plan.

How to tell if you’re close to a limit & when it refreshes

Why you might want a larger context windowA larger context window allows Gemini to read and comprehend more. For example, with a 1M token context window, Gemini can understand up to 1,500 pages of text or 30,000 lines of code.

If you exceed the context window, this could lead to responses that don’t take into account all the content provided or miss connections or details throughout the content. This is most relevant for prompts that require attention to many details scattered throughout large files.
